To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed a new method to reveal the network connectivity of dozens of neurons in the brain slice preparation by monitoring the spatiotemporally resolved firing patterns of presyaptic neuron candidates en masse with functional calcium imaging.

we developed a method to identify the presynaptic neurons that make synaptic connections onto given postsynaptic cells in situ by using a combination of functional multineuron Ca2+ imaging and patch clamping, with which we could identify the presynapatic neurons that make connections to the recorded neurons in brain slices.
we developed a novel method to unveil the synaptic network connectivity among dozens neurons in situ, and that this method can be used to probe the wiring topography in brain slice preparations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of synaptic transmission and synaptic plasticity in brain slice preparations.
the development of new techniques to study neuronal networks in the brain.
the study of the synaptic connectivity in neuronal networks.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we developed a novel technique to detect the synaptic connections among dozens of neurons with high sensitivity in brain slices.

we have developed an optical method for the identification of presynaptic partners in the intact brain, and we have used it to identify the presynaptic partners of the pyramidal neurons of the hippocampal CA1 region.
we have developed a method for identifying the presynaptic neurons of a given postsynaptic neuron, in situ, with high sensitivity and specificity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed an optical trawling technique to identify presynaptic neuron(s) that makes synaptic connections onto a given postsynaptic neuron.
we developed a novel method to unveil the synaptic connectivity in the network of neurons in situ.
we developed a new technique to identify presynaptic neuron(s) that makes synaptic connection to a postsynaptic neuron.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have developed a method to probe synaptic connectivity between neurons in a brain slice.
the combination of optical and electrophysiological methods allows for the study of synaptic connectivity at a much finer scale than has been previously possible.
we can use functional calcium imaging in brain slices to reveal the synaptic inputs onto the patch-clamp recorded neuron.
